keyTier.helpNone: The device reported that its private key is not stored in hardware-backed keystore (e.g. demo tools or software storage). This is client-reported, not attested by the server.
keyTier.helpStandard: The device reported hardware-backed keystore (e.g. Android Keystore / TEE without StrongBox). Client-reported.
keyTier.helpStrong: The device reported StrongBox or equivalent strongly isolated hardware. Client-reported.
keyTier.unknownTooltip: Not reported at verification (legacy enrollment or older client).

validation.invalidPhone: Use an international phone number with country code (example: +1 514 555 1234)
validation.invitationExpiryRequired: Choose a date and time when using a custom invitation deadline.
validation.invitationExpiryInvalid: That date and time is not valid.

detail.editContactEmailOnlyHint: Before the device binds, only the contact email can change. If an invitation already went to a wrong address, revoke this enrollment and create a new one.
detail.editExpiresHint: Applies to the pending invitation window, not a separate post-verification lifetime.
detail.errorConflict: Someone else changed this enrollment. Refresh and try again.
detail.credentialsPreviewNotice: Integrated delivery: this screen shows the enrollment proof token, binding challenge, and QR in the Admin UI so Ezkey works without email or SMS adapters. For stronger assurance, you may split them across your own channels (for example, email a screenshot of the QR and send the 6-digit binding challenge by SMS or chat). When a delivery connector is configured, this screen can also send the QR by email; the binding challenge still goes through another channel.
detail.boundChallengeWarning: A device has already scanned this enrollment. Confirm who you are speaking to before giving this code.
detail.tokenHint: Share this token with the user to set up their EZKey mobile app.
detail.qrCodeHint: User can scan this QR code with the EZKey mobile app.
detail.deactivateIntro: Deactivating temporarily prevents authentication. The enrollment can be reactivated later.
detail.reactivateIntro: This enrollment is inactive. Reactivating will restore authentication capabilities.
detail.revokeIntro: Irreversible. Revoking permanently disables this enrollment. A new enrollment must be created for re-enrolment.
detail.revokeConfirmTitle: This action is PERMANENT. The enrollment will be irreversibly revoked.
detail.deleteIntro: Deleting an enrollment permanently removes the device association. The user will no longer be able to authenticate.
detail.deleteConfirmTitle: Are you sure? This action cannot be undone.
detail.revokedAlert: This enrollment has been permanently revoked.

help.proofToken: Cryptographic token used by the mobile device to bind to this enrollment.
help.bindingChallengeCode: One-time code the device must enter to complete enrollment.

detail.testAuthBlockedTooltip: Authentication is currently blocked — the integration or tenant is inactive.

operationalWarning.message: This enrollment's parent integration or tenant is currently inactive. End-user authentication is blocked until the parent is reactivated.
operationalWarning.deactivated: This enrollment is deactivated. End-user authentication is blocked until it is reactivated.

contextHelp.deactivateContent: Deactivating temporarily suspends authentication for this enrollment without making permanent changes. The enrollment can be reactivated at any time to restore the user's access. Use this for temporary suspensions, investigations, or device loss.
contextHelp.revokeContent: Revoking permanently disables this enrollment. The user's device key association is invalidated and cannot be reactivated — a new enrollment will be required to re-enrol the user. Use this when the device is lost, stolen, or compromised. A reason is required for the audit trail.
contextHelp.deleteContent: Deleting completely removes the enrollment record. This action is permanent. A reason is required for the audit trail. Prefer revoke (which preserves audit history) over delete for most security actions. Delete is typically reserved for test data cleanup or GDPR-style erasure requests.

emailDelivery.title: Send by email
emailDelivery.languageNote: The email is written in {{language}}, the language of your Admin UI. It carries the QR only, never the 6-digit code.
emailDelivery.noContactEmail: Add a contact email to send this QR by email. The QR stays available on screen.
emailDelivery.accepted: Email sent to {{email}}. Next: give the person their 6-digit code through another channel, since it is not in the email. They scan the QR, then enter the code right away. If the address was wrong, revoke this enrollment and create a new one.
emailDelivery.unknown: The email may have left for {{email}}, but the provider did not confirm it. Check with the person before sending again. The QR stays on screen.
emailDelivery.rejected: The email did not leave ({{code}}). Nothing was sent. You can show the QR on screen instead, or try again later.

refused.connectorUnavailable: Email delivery is not available right now. Show the QR on screen instead.
refused.localeNotOffered: The connector has no email in this language. Switch the Admin UI language, or show the QR on screen.
refused.notCreated: This enrollment no longer waits for a device, so its QR cannot be sent.
refused.expired: This invitation has expired. Create a new enrollment.
refused.adminEnrollment: Administrator enrollments are not sent by email. Use the onboarding screen of the administrator.
refused.parentNotOperational: The integration or tenant is not operational, so nothing can be sent.
refused.contactEmailMissing: This enrollment has no contact email. Add one first.
refused.contactEmailInvalid: The contact email is not valid. Correct it first.
refused.expectedServerMissing: The server address for the app is not configured (ezkey.qr.auth-base-url), so the email could not name it.
refused.dailyCapReached: The daily sending limit is reached. Show the QR on screen, or try again tomorrow.
refused.other: The email could not be sent. Show the QR on screen instead.

lifecycleDialog.deactivateMessage: Temporarily deactivate this enrollment? The user will not be able to authenticate until reactivated.
lifecycleDialog.reactivateMessage: Reactivate this enrollment? The user will be able to authenticate again.

testAuth.title: Test Authentication
testAuth.intro: Trigger a live authentication request for enrollment {{name}}. The end-user will see a pending request on their EZKey mobile app.
testAuth.challengeHint: A 2-digit code is displayed here. The user must confirm the matching code on their device.
testAuth.contextMessagePlaceholder: e.g. Authorize payment of $500 CAD to a supplier (Montreal).
testAuth.challengeHintLive: Show this to the user — they must confirm the matching code on their device.
testAuth.abandonHint: Close this dialog without cancelling the attempt on the server. The request stays active until it expires or the user responds on their device.
testAuth.doneAccepted: Authentication accepted! The user confirmed the request on their device. The enrollment is working correctly.
testAuth.doneRejected: Authentication rejected. The user declined the request on their device.
testAuth.doneExpired: Timed out. No response was received before the attempt expired.
testAuth.doneInvalid: Invalid attempt. The request was marked invalid — this may indicate a device binding issue.
testAuth.doneCancelled: Cancelled. The test authentication was cancelled.
